newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Shares gain against T-bills on Lithuania bourse.
newsitem.headline: Shares gain against T-bills on Lithuania bourse.

text.p: Blue chips shares continued to rise in higher volume on Lithuania's bourse on Thursday, and dealers remained bullish on the prospects for equities as investors switched back from T-bills.
Overall market volume was 753,000 litas compared with 310,000 litas on Tuesday, and the secondary T-bill bill market accounted for over half the turnover.

Dealers said investors had been turning to shares after a sharp fall in T-bill yields. Over 387,000 litas worth of one and three month T-bills were traded and yields ranged from 9.50 percent to 10.35 percent.
Central market volume was just over 298,000 litas and dealers said their informal indices charted steady blue chip gains. Lithuania has not yet introduced a formal index.
Cardboard factory Medienos Ploshas accounted for the lion's share of central market activity at 197,000 litas, rising by 2.11 percent from 9.50 litas to 9.70 litas.
Market leader Vilniaus Bank held firm at 1,100 litas after a steady rise. Twenty-seven of its shares were swapped in a deal worth over 29,000 litas.
